text:
Mike: Heads-up — eu-west GPU pool hit sustained 92%+ twice in the last 30m. Looks like lots of short spikes from multiple orgs, not one long job. Thinking of a miniburst hedging + capacity-linked refill design. Anyone seen similar patterns?
Anya: Yep saw that. Short spikes ~6-18s, then idle. Token-bucket with static burst lets them burn through headroom quickly.
Lee: Would love to avoid global hard caps. Maybe allow micro-bursts if real-time headroom exists, but retract quickly when GPUs go hot.
Jordan: Agreed. Key idea: separate "instant" credits (for micro-bursts) and steady-state refill. Instant credits are drawn from region headroom and expire fast.
SRE Lead: Curious about abuse vector: orgs could game instant credits and keep sending small requests across distributed keys. Need bounding and accounting per-org.
Mike: Good point. Proposal sketch: per-key token bucket (refill = baseline) + per-org "hedge pool" allocated dynamically from region headroom. Hedge tokens have TTL and aggressive reclaim.
Anya: Pseudocode rough sketch:
```
# capacity-aware refill pseudo
headroom = max(0, region_gpu_count * per_gpu_headroom - active_consumption)
region_pool_refill = headroom * alpha  # fraction we give out for hedges
for org in region:
  org.hedge_refill = region_pool_refill * org.weight
  key.refill += min(org.hedge_refill, key.max_hedge)
```
Lee: Need concrete limits: max_hedge per-key = X tokens or Y ms of tokens. Also a cooldown if reclaimed.
Jordan: We should derive tokens -> seconds-of-GPU by measuring avg token consumption per token. Then set max_hedge so total borrowed <= headroom * safe_factor.
InfraBot: metric eu-west/gpu_util: 92.3% (now). queue_depth: 48. kv_cache_hit: 0.14.
SRE Lead: Rollout plan idea: start with read-only hedging (dry-run counter) in eu-west for 24h, log evictions and borrow rate. Then enable low-percentage hedging (e.g., 5% of headroom) for canary orgs.
Mike: Also want fairness: combine weighted-proportional distribution with per-org safety caps. If org uses >their weight consistently, throttle to steady-state refill and force canary fallback.
Anya: Edge case: cross-region fallback when eu-west saturated but us-east has headroom. We should avoid gratuitous cross-region routing for small bursts (network/cold-cache penalty). Maybe allow cross-region hedging only for long-running requests or if latency budget allows.
Lee: Implementation details: admission service needs a quick API: CheckAdmission(key, tokens_needed, region_hint) -> {allowed: bool, reason, source: {steady, hedge, fallback}}. Keep it stateless-ish by using a small sharded region pool with consistent hashing.
Jordan: For safety, hedges are reclaimable: if region util crosses threshold, admission service emits immediate reclaim and deducts borrowed tokens from org buckets first. Reclaim reason recorded for observability.
SRE Lead: Observability: metrics per org/key: borrow_count, borrow_bytes, reclaim_count, latency_p50/p95/p99, evicted_requests. Dashboards + alerts for borrow_rate > X and reclaimed > Y.
Anya: Test ideas: synthetic mini-spike generator that exercises 5-10k keys across 100 orgs to emulate the observed pattern. Validate that hedging reduces tail latency without increasing sustained util.
Mike: Cost angle: giving hedges increases short-term throughput which may increase GPU spend if we scale up to meet persistent tails. Add cost guardrail: if projected 24h cost delta > threshold, autoscale/disable hedges automatically.
Lee: Security/abuse: require registration for hedging feature; unknown keys get much smaller instant buckets, and suspicious patterns flagged for manual review.
Jordan: TL;DR: per-key steady token bucket + dynamic per-org hedge pool sourced from region headroom, TTL'ed hedges, reclaim on high util, observability + safety caps. Rollout: dry-run -> 5% headroom -> incremental.
SRE Lead: +1 to rollout plan. Can someone write a short design doc with config knobs and metrics we will monitor? Include gating thresholds, e.g., util_reclaim=90%, max_global_hedge=0.1*headroom, per_org_cap=0.2*org_share.
Mike: I can draft the doc and a canary checklist. Will add synthetic load script.
Anya: Happy to help with the dashboards and alerts.
Lee: I'll prototype the admission API and a tiny in-memory region-pool.
Jordan: I'll handle the abuse heuristics and tests.
InfraBot: deploybot: canary/hedge-prototype deployed to staging at 2145689200 by Mike.
Mike: Thanks all — will post doc link once ready. :+1:
